key_insight: Newsroom AI can do more than summarize or rank stories: by optimizing emotional packaging, it can change whether readers approach, trust, and share news. The paper argues that these effects must be evaluated behaviorally, not just for accuracy or engagement.
problem_solved: It addresses the gap between technical optimization of news content and real human responses, especially when AI systems use emotion to influence attention and sharing. The paper asks how to verify that emotional packaging helps accurate information reach readers without unintended effects.
method: Analyze newsroom AI as a system that shapes the emotional framing of stories, not just their content.
Use behavioral evaluation to test reader responses such as approach, trust, and sharing intent.
Combine AI system design with human-centered experiments to assess whether emotional packaging supports accurate information dissemination.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights that optimizing for engagement alone is not enough when systems influence emotions and trust. It encourages building evaluation pipelines that include behavioral outcomes and communication ethics, especially in journalism and information delivery.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing news article -> emotional packaging -> reader reactions (approach/trust/share)
A split-screen comparison of neutral vs emotionally packaged headlines
An icon-based flowchart linking AI optimization, behavioral testing, and information spread
A simple chart showing how emotional tone affects trust and sharing metrics
paper_title: Emotional optimization by newsroom AI needs behavioural evaluation
